newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine tourists take rugby cannibal souvenirs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine tourists take rugby cannibal souvenirs.

text.p: Tourists in the high Andean mountains are robbing souvenirs from the site of a notorious plane crash in Argentina where rugby players had to eat their dead teammates to survive, La Nacion reported on Thursday.

Unusually low snowfalls last winter left the crashsite exposed for the first time, allowing trekkers to make off with personal belongings of the 45 passengers who came down with the plane, mountain guide Edgar Barrios said.
A Uruguayan Air Force Fairchild plane chartered by a private high school rugby team from Montevideo crashed in the Andes on the way to a match in Chile in 1972.

Suffering severe cold and, in some cases, horrible injuries, the starving survivors were forced to eat the bodies of those killed. An official search was called off after eight days, but two of the teenage rugby players made a grueling march to look for help, eventually finding a Chilean peasant.
After a 10-week ordeal, 16 survived. Their story was made into a Hollywood film, "Alive".
